hints.content: Because $\overleftrightarrow{AC}$ is tangent to the circle at point $C$, the radius going to point $C$ is perpendicular to the tangent line.  This means that the measure of $\angle ACO$ is $90^\circ$.

We know that the angles of triangle $AOC$ have to add up to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{align}
\blue{\text{m}\angle OAC} + \pink{\text{m}\angle O} + \text{m}\angle OCA &= 180\\
\blue{\text{m}\angle OAC}+ \pink{45} + 90 &= 180 \\
\blue{\text{m}\angle OAC} + 135&= 180 \\
\blue{\text{m}\angle OAC} &= 45\\
\end{align}$

question.content:
$\overleftrightarrow{AC}$ is tangent to circle $O$ at point $C$. 

**What is the measure of $\angle OAC$?**  

[[☃ input-number 1]] $^\circ$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A circle centered around point O. Segment O C is a radius of the circle. Point A lies outside the circle, and line A C is a line that could potentially be tangent to circle O. A line segment connects point A to point O and intersects the circle at point B. Line segment A O, line segment O C, and line A C create the triangle A O C. Side A O is broken into two line segments, A B and B O. Angle B O C is forty-five degrees.
